title: Move provider configuration wiring to the composition root
verify: RED: The current route transport reads TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, constructs the ProviderAdapterRegistry, and owns the lazy production singleton; the route is therefore both HTTP adapter and provider composition seam.

GREEN: Platform/composition wiring reads the existing provider configuration and constructs/supplies the registry, while createAuthenticationTransport remains injectable and route transport contains no provider secret/config reads or adapter construction; missing configuration still maps to the existing safe provider error.

VERIFY: Independently inspect the route/composition dependency boundary and run disposable runtime probes for injected provider doubles, missing configuration, both provider start paths, and client-output secret absence; then run the full project gates.

purpose: Restore the accepted composition-root/platform ownership of provider configuration without changing the provider contract or route behavior.
success_outcome: The production provider registry and its secret configuration are wired by platform/composition ownership, authentication transport receives an injected registry, and all existing provider success/failure behavior remains safe and testable.
anti_goals: Do not select a new provider SDK, change Telegram/Google protocols, rename the existing configuration contract without authority, or add another composition root.
Do not expose secrets in page data, form results, API responses, client bundles, or route errors; do not add a dev-login or role-selection bypass.
Do not change Identity & Access ownership, membership provisioning, auth-state semantics, accepted modular-monolith + SQLite architecture, or any W9 task/history artifact.

stop_conditions: Stop and route to /spec-design if provider wiring requires changing the accepted modular-monolith + SQLite architecture, adding a second composition root/service/store/event bus, or changing module ownership/topology.

Stop if the patch requires a new provider, SDK/product behavior, credential naming decision, client-visible configuration, or a change to the provider verification contract not settled by existing specs.
Stop if any W9 task card, protocol, execution evidence, semantic evidence, lifecycle, or retry history would need modification.

constraints: Preserve the existing Telegram/Google configuration values and safe missing-configuration behavior while moving ownership to platform/composition wiring.
Keep createAuthenticationTransport injectable for isolated tests; production construction may obtain its registry only from the accepted composition root/platform seam.
Use disposable injected-adapter/runtime probes and source/client-output scans; never use live credentials or expose secrets in evidence artifacts.
invariants: SvelteKit auth routes adapt requests and call injected public boundaries; they do not own provider configuration or adapter construction.
Provider secrets remain server-only and enter through the single composition root/platform configuration seam.
Provider identity normalization, safe errors, session/invitation behavior, and no-direct-persistence rules remain unchanged.
verification_targets: Existing FT-001 login/invitation regression / REQ-001 / REQ-002 / REQ-014: disposable runtime probes prove both provider starts, injected adapters, missing configuration safe error, and unchanged login/invitation transport behavior.
